description: The plot illustrates the maximum activation values across different layers in a model under a baseline condition. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 24, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Max Activation Value,” also uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at intervals of 200. Four series are plotted: “attn_output” (blue dashed line with square markers), “attn_residual” (orange dotted line with circular markers), “ffn_output” (green dash-dot line with triangular markers), and “ffn_residual” (red solid line with no markers). The “attn_residual” series begins near zero, rises sharply to approximately 1200 at layer 5, remains relatively stable between 1200 and 1400 through layer 22, and then drops precipitously after layer 22. The “ffn_output” series remains near zero except for three distinct spikes: at layer 5 (~200), layer 13 (~800), and layer 22 (~600), with the peak at layer 13. The “ffn_residual” series mirrors the “attn_residual” trend closely, starting near zero, rising sharply to ~1400 at layer 5, staying elevated until layer 22, and then falling sharply afterward, though its values are slightly lower than “attn_residual” in the plateau region. The “attn_output” series remains nearly flat near zero across all layers, with a small rise to approximately 150 at layer 22 before returning to near zero.

The 'attn_residual' series peaks sharply at layer 5, reaching approximately 1200, and remains stable between 1200 and 1400 before declining after layer 22. The 'ffn_output' series shows consistent spikes at layers 5, 13, and 22, with the largest spike at layer 13 reaching approximately 800. The 'ffn_residual' series exhibits a similar pattern to 'attn_residual,' but with slightly lower values overall. Notably, the 'attn_output' series remains flat across most layers, with a minor increase to approximately 150 at layer 22.
